author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 나그네새, 해마다 수백 마리 · 겨울에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
summary: 백두산 지역에서는 여름새이고 그 밖의 지역에서는 매우 드물게 지나가는 나그네새로, 4~5월에 와서 9월까지 머문다. 관목림이나 마을 가까운 나무에 살며, 나무 구멍이나 딱따구리가 쓰던 둥지에 6~7월 무늬 없는 흰 알을 6~10개 낳는다. 주로 동물을 먹어 딱정벌레, 벌, 나비 무리의 곤충과 거미를 잡으며, 특히 개미를 좋아한다. 날개 길이는 9cm이며, 한국, 일본, 시베리아에 분포한다.

points.en: black streaks on the upperparts, centre of back and supercilium
yellowish-grey tail with brown markings and 5–6 black bars

art.subject: Eurasian Wryneck (Jynx torquilla), adult (sexes alike, same plumage all year), as seen in Korean village shrubbery in April-May: upperparts silvery grey-brown, finely vermiculated like tree bark, with a dark brown stripe from the crown down the nape to the centre of the back and dark stripes along the scapulars forming a dark V; a dark brown stripe through the eye down the side of the neck; throat and breast buff-yellowish, finely barred dark; rest of the underparts whitish to buff with small dark arrowhead spots; long grey tail finely vermiculated, crossed by several narrow dark bars; short pointed grey-horn bill; brown eye; pale brownish legs.
art.pose: on the ground beside an ant nest, picking up ants
art.scene: Korean village outskirts with shrubs and scattered trees in late spring; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched across a branch: bark-like grey-brown upperparts with a dark crown-to-back stripe and dark scapular V, dark eye-stripe, buff finely barred throat and breast, whitish spotted belly, short pointed bill, pale brown legs
adult, tail detail from above, slightly spread: long rounded grey tail finely vermiculated brown and crossed by several narrow black bars
art.build: Small, slim, cryptic relative of the woodpeckers, a little larger and longer-tailed than a sparrow; looks like a cross between a large warbler and a nightjar. Smallish head on a flexible neck that it twists snake-like when disturbed. Bill short, straight and pointed, shorter than the head, not chisel-like. Legs short, pale brownish, with two toes forward and two back. Perches across branches like a songbird and feeds on the ground on ants; does not climb trunks with the tail braced. Wings short and rounded; the long, soft, rounded tail extends well beyond the wingtips.
avoid: Do not paint it clinging upright on a trunk propped on a stiff tail like a woodpecker; it perches across branches or hops on the ground.
Do not paint black-and-white or red woodpecker colours, or a chisel bill.
Do not paint a crest or a plain unpatterned back.
Do not paint a pure white unmarked underside; the throat and breast are buff and barred.
